# t.must is an assert that stops the test where it fails.
#
# The Go lowering answered only t.assert and wrote a comment for t.must, so a
# local read only by a must was declared and not used and the test program
# failed to build, and a must that held nothing passed.

! sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
! sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
! stdout 'assert failed'
! sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
! stdout 'assert failed'
! sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'must failed: \(s.N == 2\)'
! stdout 'assert failed'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct S {
    n int
}

func testMustHolds(t test.Test) {
    var s = S{n=1}
    t.must(s.n == 1)
}

func testMustStops(t test.Test) {
    var s = S{n=1}
    t.must(s.n == 2)
    t.assert(s.n == 3)
}

ui.window {
    ui.text(value="x")
}
